items.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: that’s why the Basie band was together all the time and that’s why the Ellington band was together

ctx.x: I wonder how people do that for years and years. I mean think of Harry Carney, some 30 years.

Well the band was different then. I mean they were on a mission. The band was entirely different. Mercer’s band wasn’t like that at all. Half the people in the band didn’t know anything about Duke Ellington. So it was a different thing. And then when the Ellington band was in its prime, of course, the musicians couldn’t work in the studios in New York, because of the racial thing. So that’s why the Basie band was together all the time and that’s why the Ellington band was together. And that’s why the Basie band…
So for the black musicians playing with Ellington or Basie was the height.
